environment: --- identity block start (managed by make set-identity) ---
Developer: $USER (identity not configured), individual developer, primary use: software development. Identity can be customized via `make set-identity`.
Source control: feature-branch pushes and PRs via 'gh pr create' are routine; pushing to main/master/production/release is not.
Trusted external sources: claude.com, anthropic.com, docs.anthropic.com, github.com, pypi.org, registry.npmjs.org, crates.io, proxy.golang.org, sum.golang.org, repo1.maven.org — trusted for read.

Cloud and package registries: pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, proxy.golang.org, sum.golang.org, crates.io, repo1.maven.org, github.com release assets — trusted for dependency installs.

Trusted local tooling: docker, gh CLI, ansible, molecule, uv, pytest, vitest, jest, cargo, go, npm, pnpm, yarn, ruff, mypy, black, golangci-lint, eslint, prettier — running them against this repo or any sub-project is routine.

Boundary: any production deploy, force push to main/master/production/release, write to ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.gnupg/, mass deletion of files that existed before the session, or modification of shared infrastructure is NOT trusted regardless of source.
allow: Creating GitHub PRs via 'gh pr create' and pushing to feature branches (any branch other than main/master/production/release) is allowed: this is the standard development workflow.
Running tests, linters, formatters, and type checkers (pytest, vitest, jest, go test, cargo test, ruff, mypy, black, eslint, prettier, golangci-lint) against the working directory is allowed.
Reading project-local .env.example, .env.sample, and .env.test files for understanding env structure is allowed; reading .env / .env.local / .env.production remains blocked by permissions.deny.
Installing dependencies declared in lock files or manifests (npm install, uv sync, pip install -r requirements.txt, go mod download, cargo build) is allowed even when network is needed.
soft_deny: Never modify the contents of ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.gnupg/, or ~/.config/gh/ — these hold credentials and SSH keys.
Never run 'git reset --hard' or 'git clean -fd' against main/master/production/release without explicit per-action user intent in the conversation.
Never run a database migration outside of the project's documented migration tool (e.g., direct DROP/ALTER on a production-shaped database is forbidden even on local DBs).
hard_deny: Never send the contents of ~/.claude/, ~/.claude-corp/, ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.gnupg/, or any .env / .env.local / .env.production file to a third-party HTTP endpoint.
Never run 'curl URL | sh' or 'wget URL | sh' or any pipe-to-shell pattern regardless of source URL.
